# Piglet lifecycle

A Piglet goes through nine stages, from a YAML file you write to an agent that other people install and update. This page names each stage. It gives one command for each stage and states what the command changes.

[Piglets](piglets.md) explain the file. [Piglet Binaries](https://pi-in-go.dev/docs/latest/piglet-binaries) explain the executable. [Publish a Package or Piglet](publishing.md) explains npm publication.

```text
author -> validate -> run -> inspect -> register -> build -> sign and verify -> publish -> install and update
  file      check     try     look      copy to     script    key, signature,   GitHub     add, pull,
            schema    it      at it     ~/.pig      or        trust             Release    update
                                        /piglets    Binary                      or npm
```

## The stages at a glance

| Stage | Command | What it changes | Release record |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Author | Edit the YAML file. `pig piglet schema` prints the schema. | Your file. | No record. |
| 2. Validate | `pig piglet validate <name\|path>` | Nothing. | No record. |
| 3. Run | `pig --piglet <name\|path>` | Nothing on disk, except the Session you create. | No record. |
| 4. Inspect | `pig piglet show <name\|path>` | Nothing. | Lists the records that exist. |
| 5. Register | `pig piglet add <path\|npm:ref\|git:ref>` | Copies the file into `~/.pig/piglets/`. A remote source also writes `<name>.origin.json`. | The origin file records the source, the resolved version and the digest. |
| 6. Build | `pig piglet build <name> --format script\|binary --out <path>` | Writes the script or the Binary. | A Binary writes a record. A script writes none. |
| 7. Sign and verify | `pig piglet keygen`, `build --sign-key`, `pig piglet verify` | Adds a signature to the Binary. | The signature covers the record. |
| 8. Publish | `pig piglet publish <name\|path> --to github\|npm` | Creates a GitHub Release or an npm package. A dry run changes nothing. | Writes a publication receipt. |
| 9. Install and update | `pig piglet add npm:<name>`, `pig piglet pull <release>`, `pig piglet update <name>` | Installs the Piglet source or the signed Binary. | Pins the signer and keeps the signed index. |

Planned stages are marked in the sections below and in [Planned stages](#planned-stages).

## 1. Author

Write one YAML file. Only `name` is required. This file limits the built-in tools to a read-only set:

```yaml
name: reviewer
description: A read-only code reviewer.
tools: [read, grep, find]
systemPrompt:
  text: Review the code. Do not change files.
release:
  version: 0.1.0
```

Print the closed schema of the file:

```bash
pig piglet schema
```

`release.version` is the version of the Piglet release. Set it before you build or publish. See [Piglets](piglets.md) for every field.

## 2. Validate

```bash
pig piglet validate ./reviewer.yaml
```

```text
OK: reviewer (./reviewer.yaml): 0 extension(s), 0 skill(s)
```

Validation checks the schema. It also resolves every origin. It changes nothing.

## 3. Run

```bash
pig --piglet ./reviewer.yaml
```

This starts PiG with the Piglet from the file. The Piglet does not become the default. A bare `pig` still runs Stock PiG.

## 4. Inspect

```bash
pig piglet show ./reviewer.yaml
```

```text
Piglet: reviewer
  A read-only code reviewer.
Source: ./reviewer.yaml
Built-in tools: read, grep, find (a limit; it does not activate a tool)
Active by default: read

System prompt: Review the code. Do not change files. (37 bytes)

Release:
  version: 0.1.0
```

In an interactive session, an active Piglet adds the read-only command `/piglet`.

### Piglet tool scope

The `tools` list is a ceiling. The Piglet keeps at most the tools in the list. A run activates only the default tools that the list keeps. In the example, `Active by default` is `read`, because `grep` and `find` are not default tools.

The Piglet scope removes tools from the tool registry of the Session. This is the registry that `--tools` and `--exclude-tools` also filter. A tool that the scope removes is gone. The model cannot call it. A `codemode` script cannot call it. `tool_search` cannot find it. See [Tool scope](piglets.md#tool-scope) for the rules for extension tools and MCP tools.

## 5. Register

Copy the file into your Piglet directory so that you can select it by name:

```bash
pig piglet add ./reviewer.yaml
pig piglet list
pig --piglet reviewer
```

```text
Added reviewer (0 extensions, 0 skills) → ~/.pig/piglets/reviewer.yaml
NAME      SCOPE  SOURCE                      BINARY  IMAGE  DESCRIPTION
reviewer  user   ~/.pig/piglets/reviewer.yaml  -       -      A read-only code reviewer.
```

`pig piglet add` also takes a remote source:

```bash
pig piglet add npm:@acme/review@^1.0.0
pig piglet add git:https://github.com/acme/review.git@v2.0.0
```

A remote source writes `<name>.origin.json` next to the Piglet. The file records the exact version or commit and the digest. See [Validate and register](https://pi-in-go.dev/docs/latest/piglets#validate-and-register).

## 6. Build

A script is a thin launcher. A Piglet Binary is one executable that contains PiG and the Piglet:

```bash
pig piglet build reviewer --format script --out ./run-reviewer
pig piglet build reviewer --format binary --out ./pig-reviewer
```

A script writes no record. A Binary writes a record and a managed copy under `~/.pig/receipts/piglets/` and `~/.pig/artifacts/piglets/`. `pig piglet show reviewer` lists them after the build:

```text
Piglet Binaries:
  linux/amd64  version=0.1.0  build-checks-passed=true
    record=~/.pig/receipts/piglets/reviewer/<source digest>/0.1.0/piglet-binary/linux-amd64/<record>.json
    artifact=~/.pig/artifacts/piglets/reviewer/<source digest>/0.1.0/linux-amd64/<digest>/pig-reviewer
```

The native builder compiles PiG with the Go toolchain on your computer. See [Build outputs](https://pi-in-go.dev/docs/latest/piglets#build-outputs) for the builders and their prerequisites.

### Overlay Piglets

A Piglet Binary runs its own Piglet only. It refuses `--piglet`, `PIG_PIGLET_PATH` and `PIG_PIGLET_NAME`. To let a Binary accept one more Piglet at launch, set `build.allowOverlays` in the Piglet that you build:

```yaml
name: pig-base
tools: [read, grep, find]
build:
  allowOverlays: true
systemPrompt:
  text: Base.
```

The Binary then takes an overlay with `--piglet`:

```bash
pig piglet build ./base.yaml --format binary --out ./pig-base
./pig-base --piglet ./extra.yaml
```

An overlay merges onto the Piglet of the Binary exactly as an `extends` child merges onto its base. An overlay file has an `extends` block with no `source`. Stock `pig piglet validate` rejects such a file by design, because it has no base to extend:

```text
FAIL: Piglet extra.yaml: extends.source is required unless a Piglet Binary that sets build.allowOverlays runs the Piglet as an overlay
```

An overlay can replace the system prompt. It can remove members with `extends.remove`. It can widen the ceilings only with `extends.allowWiden: true`.

The Binary refuses only the parts that its build compiled in. It names the field and the reason. Two examples:

```text
remove.strip.extensions: "mcp" is absent
strip.extensions: "mcp" is compiled out of Piglet Binary "pig-nomcp" (build tag pig_strip_mcp), so its code is not in the Binary; an overlay cannot re-enable it
```

The first message means that the Binary does not strip `mcp`, so the overlay has nothing to remove. The second message means that the build removed the `mcp` code from the executable. An overlay cannot bring that code back. See [Accept overlay Piglets](https://pi-in-go.dev/docs/latest/piglet-binaries#accept-overlay-piglets) for the full rules.

`build.allowOverlays` is part of the baked Piglet. A change to it changes the Piglet digest in the record.

## 7. Sign and verify

Create an Ed25519 key pair once. Keep the private file secret and publish the `.pub` file:

```bash
pig piglet keygen ./reviewer-signing.key
```

Sign during the build:

```bash
pig piglet build reviewer --format binary --out ./pig-reviewer --sign-key ./reviewer-signing.key
```

Check the file without running it:

```bash
pig verify ./pig-reviewer
pig piglet verify ./pig-reviewer --source reviewer
```

```text
Piglet Binary: ./pig-reviewer
Signature: signed by ed25519:<key-id> (not in your Piglet trust store: this proves it is unchanged since that key signed it, not who holds the key)
Provenance: matches ~/.pig/piglets/reviewer.yaml
Signed manifest:
  Piglet: reviewer 0.1.0
  target: linux/amd64
  Pig: 0.5.3
  Piglet definition: sha256:<digest>
  resolution record: sha256:<digest>
  component plan: sha256:<digest>
  executable: sha256:<digest> (<size> bytes)
```

To attach a local identity to a key, trust it. To require signatures, turn the policy on:

```bash
pig piglet trust add ./reviewer-signing.key.pub
pig piglet trust list
pig piglet trust require on
```

See [Sign a Binary](https://pi-in-go.dev/docs/latest/piglet-binaries#sign-a-binary).

## What changes the release record

The signed manifest above names the parts of the release record. Each edit changes one or more of them:

| You change | What changes |
|---|---|
| `release.version` | The version in the record path, the GitHub tag `v<release.version>`, and the npm version. |
| The Piglet file | The source digest. The record path contains the source digest, so a new source gets a new record. |
| A prompt file, a skill, or a base Piglet that the Piglet names | The Piglet definition digest. `pig piglet verify --source` fails until you rebuild. |
| The extensions or their origins | The component plan and the resolution record. |
| `build.allowOverlays` | The Piglet definition digest. |
| The target (`--targets`) | A separate record and Binary for each target. |
| The PiG version that builds the Binary | The `Pig:` line of the manifest. |

A script never has a record. Rebuild a Binary after every change in this table.

## 8. Publish

Publish signed Binaries to a GitHub Release:

```bash
pig piglet publish reviewer --to github --repo acme/reviewer --sign-key ./reviewer-signing.key
```

Publish the source to npm:

```bash
pig piglet publish ./reviewer.yaml --to npm
```

Both commands are dry runs until you add `--yes`. The GitHub command uses the GitHub CLI (`gh`). It stops with an error when `gh` is not on `PATH`. The npm dry run prints the package that it would publish:

```text
Piglet: reviewer@0.1.0 (not on npm yet)
Signed Binary: none recorded
...
Would run: npm publish /tmp/pig-piglet-npm-<id> --ignore-scripts
Dry run only; rerun with --yes to publish.
```

npm refuses a version that exists. Raise `release.version` before you publish again. See [Publish to GitHub Releases](https://pi-in-go.dev/docs/latest/piglet-binaries#publish-to-github-releases) and [Publish a Package or Piglet](publishing.md).

## 9. Install and update

A user installs the source from npm or Git. A user installs a signed Binary from a GitHub Release:

```bash
pig piglet add npm:@acme/review@^1.0.0
pig piglet pull github:acme/reviewer@0.1.0
pig piglet update reviewer
```

`pig piglet pull` verifies the signed release index, the signature of the Binary and the checksums before it installs anything. The first pull pins the signer. A later signer change needs `--accept-signer <key-id>`.

`pig piglet update <name>` updates a signed GitHub Binary that `pig piglet pull` installed. It stays inside the signed namespace of that Binary. It does not update a source Piglet. See [Pull a published Binary](https://pi-in-go.dev/docs/latest/piglet-binaries#pull-a-published-binary).

## Planned stages

These commands do not work in this release. Each one fails with a clear message and writes nothing:

| Planned | Today |
|---|---|
| `pig piglet pull <name>`, a pull by installed Piglet name | `pig piglet pull` needs a release index URL or a GitHub release reference. |
| `pig piglet build <name> --format image` (a Piglet Image) | Fails with `Piglet Image build is not implemented`. |
| `pig piglet build <name> --locked` | Fails with `--locked and --record Piglet artifact builds are not implemented`. |
| `pig piglet build <name> --record <path>` | The same failure as `--locked`. |

See [Planned stages in Piglets](piglets.md#planned-not-in-this-release-named-pulls-and-image-artifacts).
